pr_title: Cache asset ASTs and reuse in packagers, scope hoisting source maps
pr_body:
This stores ASTs for each asset in the cache and reuses them when needed in packager plugins. Previously, the scope hoisting packager needed to re-parse every asset and re-generate at the end, and we didn't support source maps because it was hard to preserve and combine the source maps of many assets correctly.

Now the final `generate` step in transformation happens lazily: when `getCode()` is called in the packager. If `getAST()` is called, in case of scope hoisting, then generating only happens on the final bundle. Because we are combining ASTs in scope hoisting now rather than re-parsing, we get source maps "for free".

Closes #1564.

To do:

- [x] Cache the results of `getCode` when it generates from an AST
- [x] Figure out where to load the generate plugin relative from
- [x] Figure out how to compute asset size when we don't generate code
- [x] Expose dirty status from AST to plugins?
- [x] Clear code when AST is set?

@wbinnssmith Have you tested/improved the performance of this? Is it actually faster now?

@mischnic It's not faster, but it's not slower. It was about 30% slower in the stress test until I added conditional generation at the end of transformation if it's not js or not scopehoisting.

The reason it was slower when not using scope hoisting is that there's a tendency for a entry bundles to be much larger than others, and most of the generation occurred in one thread producing that, whereas before it was better distributed across workers during transformation.

I'm going to mark this final to-do as complete as it seems we've decided to use sourcemap information to report on asset size when bundling completes. 

We also use asset size as a heuristic for extracting common bundles during bundling. For tree-shaken builds, this seems difficult to do accurately. See #4368.

issue_context.title: Add support for source maps with tree shaking
issue_context.body:
Source maps are currently unsupported with tree shaking. Because of the way we concatenate the ASTs, and the ordering required, the existing source map infrastructure was insufficient to implement this easily for the first release.

There are a couple ways we could make this work:

1. We could use the source map generated by babel in the concatenate transform and map back to the original source maps generated for each file.
2. We could attempt to share the original ASTs of each file into the cache so we wouldn't need to parse it again in the packager. These ASTs have the original source map info embedded in them as well, so when we concatenate the ASTs together we can generate a combined source map automatically as well via babel. This option will require some performance testing to see how slow it is to pass the whole AST back over the IPC from workers vs passing generated code.

Looks like we would discard a previous sourcemap in this case?
I took a look at `@babel/parser` and there doesn't seem to be an option to pass along an existing sourcemap when parsing. Does Babel read and use a sourcemap comment when parsing?

Apparently only `require("@babel/core").transform*` parses the comment (which wouldn't really work here either).
If we indeed use swc for env, this would be rather important.

For now, I'm ok with merging as is. In order to do this properly, we'd need to parse the source map and code, traverse all AST nodes, and map their source location through the source map. At the moment, this case should never happen unless you replace the JSTransformer or put a transformer after it that returns a string instead of an AST. I think that should be fairly rare, so we can address this later if it comes up.

~As I understand, the code in `Transformation.js#runTransformer` uses the last transformer with a generate function, so this is actually not needed?~

But that would require this transformer to be run after a transformer that does contain the parse/generate code for Babel.
I guess the only solution would be a shared `@parcel/ast-babel` as an abstraction...
Yeah I think Babel parse+generate code is duplicated here and across the JS and Babel transformers. A shared library would make sense.
I think adding `return` after `logger.warn(errorToDiagnostic(err));` would fix CI.

- Generally, when would getAST return a nullish value? Should this be an assertion?
- We should probably add the checks that are in `parse` here well?

The Babel Transformer itself doesn't parse at all, instead using the ast if it's available from a prior transformer and sending the code as a string through babel [0]

[0] https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/e75bad2ff98eea4a02290bd74d71d1f77131e68e/packages/transformers/babel/src/babel7.js#L57

Seems fine for now, but this is somewhat plugin specific. Other packager plugins may utilize cached ASTs than just scope hoisting in the future. We may want to parallelize generate calls from within packagers too at some point.
So if you call getAST multiple times, this would repeatedly deserialize it from cache?
Yeah, this is true of `getMap` as well. We should address this.
